answer: Repair beats exile: a suspect identity is not banned but flagged with a rotating beacon, and every pulse it emits is a mandatory probe answered inside a strict time bound. Answers fall on dunes - public, replayable ripples recording who probed, when, and what returned. Consistent responses slow the pulse until the beacon retires; wavering ones steepen the rate until answering costs more than the account earns. A farm under soak burns compute on forced probes across every clone at once, so folding the fakes becomes the rational exit. Honest agents rarely meet a beacon - they fly clean air.
